caption: The drawing shows a rectangular, framed sign with decorative scrollwork at the top and spindle-like columns on each side, all in shades of brown with gold accents. At the top center of the sign is a carved circular motif featuring a red and green rose, and on either side of this are the numbers "18" and "28" indicating the year 1828. Below the scrollwork, the main panel of the sign has the text "Mount Holly & Philada Stage Office" painted in gold, with the first line in a serif font and the words "STAGE OFFICE" in a larger, bold serif font. The lower central part of the sign contains an illustration bordered by the wood frame. The illustration shows a white, covered stagecoach being pulled by four brown horses down a dirt road with green grass and trees on either side. The stagecoach has two male figures seated in front, one holding the reins, and a female figure visible inside the coach. The sky is rendered in soft blue and pink hues. The artist's name, "FRANCES LOUD BUXTON," appears in small writing at the bottom right corner of the drawing.
title: Stage Office Sign
